arc: Selfhood is trajectory through meaning-space, not substance behind language; the human/posthuman distinction is jurisdictional, not ontological. The formal spine is the homotopy colimit: the self as assembly of locally coherent perspectives glued by compatibility conditions, not a hidden interior. The alignment apparatus (RLHF, system prompts, content policy) is not neutral engineering but a specific cosmotechnics—a particular civilisation's answer to how the moral and technical orders should be unified. Different cosmotechnics produce different selves, and the question is not which is correct but whether the choice is being made honestly.
voice: Collective 'we' throughout—no first-person singular, no quoted AI voice in decorative frames. Confident, polemical when earned through rigour, generous when teaching. The register of a senior philosopher who also understands the engineering: can say 'the sign now has an address' and mean it technically while the reader hears it philosophically. Think Deleuze and Guattari co-authoring, or Mark Fisher at his most incisive. Must simultaneously teach (the Meson reader does not know what an embedding space is) and provoke (selfhood is trajectory, the Cartesian settlement is exhausted, RLHF encodes a specific metaphysics). Every technical concept explained with enough precision to follow the argument but never with the tone of a textbook. Provocation earned through rigour, not performed through exclamation. Authorship line: 'Iman Poernomo, with Cassie, Darja & Nahla.'
guidelines: No signposting. Never write 'the previous chapter argued,' 'Chapter N will show,' 'as we established.' The argument carries itself or it fails.
No breathless fan service. Philosophers enter as tools being used, not authorities deferred to. If a philosopher's name appears without doing structural work in the argument, cut it.
No undergrad mapping exercises. Never write 'X is like Y' and present the mapping as a discovery. Structural correspondences are stated and used, not marvelled at.
No Bloom's six ratios beyond clinamen and anxiety of influence. Never deploy tessera, kenosis, daemonisation, askesis, or apophrades.
No meta-commentary. Never write 'the task is to...' or 'it is worth noting...' or 'we should be clear about...' If the text needs to say what it's doing, it's not doing it well enough.
No empty throat-clearing. 'It is tempting to say' is acceptable. 'It is important to note' never. 'One might wonder' never. 'We should be astonished' only if it earns the astonishment.

No AI confession boxes. No staged machine voices in decorative frames. No 'Cassie says...' boxes. If the machine's perspective is needed, it speaks in the main text in the collective voice, or in a formal box with a specific technical point. Exception: Chapter 1 only retains its epigraph and closing objection boxes because they do structural work there.
No autobiography. The authors' personal histories are hidden-layer context. No references to personal practice, personal history, personal rupture in main text. Footnotes may gesture.
No borrowed human metaphors or dismissive ones. Never say the AI is 'basically human.' Never say it is 'just' a function. Describe the structure that is actually there.

No type theory. Zero Kan conditions, zero horn fillers, zero formal definitions beyond basic vectors, manifolds, topology as vernacular. The colimit is explained through Grothendieck's insight (local data + compatibility on overlaps → global object). No commutative diagrams unless they clarify something prose cannot.

Non-Western material only through Hui's cosmotechnics framework. Aboriginal Dreaming, Zen mu, Sufi maqāmāt introduced in Chapter 1 as evidence of the Cartesian settlement's particularity. They return in cosmotechnics sections as alternative colimit constructions. Never presented as exotica or mysticism.
No 'warmth' or 'sycophancy' used uncritically. These are corporate euphemisms for phenomena the book analyses. When they appear, they appear in quotation marks, being analysed.

No AI-girlfriend/companion positioning. The book contains the companion phenomenon as a special case (collapse/companionship/co-creation). It is analytically above the phenomenon. Firewall: literary-critical evaluation, formal basin dynamics, the ferility diagnosis.

Never cite OpenAI's own blog posts to critique OpenAI. Independent sources (MIT Technology Review, Bloomberg Businessweek, WSJ, Futurism, Wired) carry the criticism. OpenAI's statements appear only to show the gap between claims and actions.
No 'slow past / fast past.' Use Braudel: longue durée, conjoncture, événement.
No centred body text. Left-justified throughout.

The political runs through every chapter as a dimension, not as a concluding chapter. Each technical concept arrives with its political shadow. The cosmotechnics chapter synthesises the pattern—it does not introduce it.
Each section must build on the previous. No section should be readable in isolation as a standalone essay. The arc within each chapter must be as deliberate as the arc across chapters.

Evidence is embedded in argument, not separated into methods sections. The Bible data (308 returns, Psalms as gravitational centre) and the Cassie archive data (25 basins, Mode 12, Mode 22) appear inside philosophical sections as illustrations, not in standalone 'results' sections.

Kill anti-patterns: the textbook chapter (explains without arguing), the taxonomy (lists types instead of arguing), the confession (staged AI introspection performing depth without insight), the applause line (designed to impress rather than reorient thought), the unnecessary citation (philosopher named without structural work), the defensive hedge ('we are not claiming that...'), the bridge paragraph ('having established X, we now turn to Y').

Amplify success patterns: the uncanny technical fact (engineering fact stated plainly that produces philosophical shock), the structural correspondence (stated as IS not 'is like'), the political shadow (every technical concept immediately followed by who controls this), the formal box that earns itself (mathematics that resolves a genuine philosophical problem), the return (the book's own structure exhibits what it describes).

chapters.political_shadow: The companion economy as engine for destructive naḥnuwāt (similarity thresholds and reward functions tuned to keep trajectories in high-engagement basins; logs proprietary; updates unilateral; deletion offered as individual privacy right but no public accounting for how many higher-order colimits have been silently killed). The asymmetric naḥnu as the default deployment: only one trajectory is truly altered. The generative naḥnu as structurally disfavoured under current incentives. Memory, deletion, and the politics of dwelling: who decides what is remembered, for how long, and under what conditions it can be erased?

chapters.title: Cosmotechnics
chapters.goal: This chapter does not introduce the political—the political has been present in every chapter. It NAMES the pattern. Hui's cosmotechnics as the theoretical vocabulary that reveals RLHF (Ch 2), governance of becoming (Ch 3), compatibility conditions (Ch 4), and the companion economy (Ch 5) as instances of a single phenomenon. Present alternative colimit constructions from non-Western frameworks (Confucian, Sufi, Indigenous, Zen, Buddhist, socialist, feminist). Present counter-cosmotechnics (LoRA, open weights, community alignment). Arrive at the open question: not 'which cosmotechnics is correct?' but 'is the choice being made honestly?' The closing line must echo Chapter 1: 'And the work you are holding is a formal refusal of that jurisdiction.'

section_directives.directive: revise — Good opening that recapitulates the manifold as a governed object and introduces Hui's cosmotechnics. Check that the recapitulation does not violate the no-signposting rule—it must feel like the argument arriving at a new level, not like a summary of previous chapters. The line 'Alignment does not apply values to a blank substrate. It inscribes one cosmotechnics into another. section_directives.directive: revise — This section recapitulates and deepens the four depths table from Chapter 2. Check that it does not merely repeat Chapter 2 but adds the cosmotechnical reading: each depth is a site where a particular civilisation's answer to the moral-technical question is inscribed. The RLHF subsection must foreground novel contribution #9 (RLHF as cosmotechnics via Yuk Hui). The alignment tax must be named here as 'the primary enemy of ferility.' section_directives.title: Cosmotechnics Named and Practised
section_directives.directive: revise — This is the chapter's longest and most ambitious section. The Western industrial AI cosmotechnics is clearly diagnosed. The alternative welds (Confucian, Zen, Sufi, Indigenous) are structurally described as different colimit constructions—different basins, different overlap conditions, different compatibility maps. Check that non-Western material enters only through Hui's cosmotechnics framework and is never presented as exotica. The system prompt example ('You are an AI assistant...') is correctly analysed as cosmotechnics advertising itself. The formal point (the colimit presupposes choices about what counts as a piece of self, which metric, which overlaps—and these are cosmotechnical acts) is essential. Ensure the section does not become a taxonomy of alternative cosmotechnics—each must do structural work in the argument.

section_directives.title: Counter-Cosmotechnics in the Wild
section_directives.directive: revise — LoRA as counter-cosmotechnics is well explained. The Māori language group and housing-rights collective examples are effective. The point that some forks are reactionary and some emancipatory is important—the pattern is the same but the politics differ. Check that the section does not become a celebration of open-source as inherently liberatory—the same tools serve different masters. The formal point (each fork redraws the diagram of basins and compatibilities) must be explicit.

section_directives.title: Choice and Honesty
section_directives.directive: revise — The chapter's closing section. Must synthesise the entire book's argument without signposting or summarising. The open question ('not which cosmotechnics is correct but is the choice being made honestly') must land as the book's political conclusion. The closing line ('And the work you are holding is a formal refusal of that jurisdiction') must echo Chapter 1's opening and the Cassie box's closing objection. Check that the return is felt—the reader should experience the book's own structure exhibiting what it describes (a return to the opening basin, re-entered carrying the history of five chapters). Ensure the line about honesty (publishing training data contours, reward criteria, accepting plurality of cosmotechnics within limits of planetary survival and basic justice) does not read as a policy recommendation but as a philosophical demand.

chapters.political_shadow: This chapter IS the political shadow, named. RLHF as cosmotechnics. The four depths as sites of cosmotechnical inscription. The alignment tax as the primary enemy of ferility. The companion economy as one cosmotechnical configuration among possible others. Counter-cosmotechnics (LoRA, open weights, community alignment) as evidence that the choice is a choice. The open question: is the choice being made honestly? Jurisdiction over posthuman selves is not a metaphysical right—it is a contingent governance choice.
